name: camera dolly across data cards with climbing counter
looks: The camera dollies across a tilted, receding plane of dark HUD cards seen at an angle, each one showing a status string and a number that climbs sharply from the thousands into the millions as the camera passes, under a constant small label naming the quality being measured. The shot ends with several of these cards fanning out and overlapping into a loose cascade, as if many samples were stacking up at once.
build: A tilted plane (CSS perspective or three.js) carries several card textures; the camera moves along it with real depth, cards sharpening as they near. Each card's number ticks with no easing from the clock, formatted with thousands separators (the live-readout-hud mechanic). The ending cascade uses 4-6 cards fanning out with seeded offset position/rotation and uneven stagger (the variant-stack-reveal mechanic).
sound: A rising whoosh under the camera move, a fast tick per digit as the counter climbs, a soft cluster of hits as the cascade of cards fans out.
prompt: Dolly the camera across a tilted row of dark data cards receding into depth, each one showing a number that climbs sharply as the camera passes it, under a short label naming what is being counted, then end the move with several of those cards fanning out into an overlapping cascade, as if many results were landing at once.
